header:
Date: 2026-10-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Evan Rogers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Head of ML, Astra), Tom Cheng (CTO, Astra), Ravi Kapoor (Senior Data Engineer, Astra)
summary: Discovery focused on embeddings + reranking architecture. Astra currently evaluating vector DB options and whether to run on Redwood hosted API versus dedicated pools or private deployment. Key concerns: throughput (500 qps target), dimensionality (1536 vs 768), hybrid search with BM25+ANN, data residency and encryption/KMS, integration with their existing Elastic/Opensearch stack. Agreed next steps: share pricing, benchmark playbook, and schedule pilot for 1M vectors.
topics: Current stack and pain points; Embedding model selection and dimensionality; Vector DB integration options (hosted vs self-managed); Reranking architecture (2-stage: sparse retrieval + ANN embeddings + cross-encoder rerank); Throughput and latency targets; Dedicated capacity and autoscaling; Security (SOC2, KMS, VPC); Pilot scope and success criteria.
questions: How does Redwood handle hybrid search (BM25 + ANN) latency trade-offs? What dimensionality do you recommend for our use-case (short logistics queries)? Can we run vector store locally while using Redwood hosted embeddings? What's required for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment and typical lead time?
transcript:
[00:00] Evan Rogers: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan from Redwood, with Priya our SE. Quick intros?
[00:08] Marta Lopez: Hi, Marta here, head of ML at Astra, we run route optimization and docs search for drivers.
[00:13] Tom Cheng: Tom here, CTO, I'm mostly listening but want to understand ops and cost.
[00:18] Ravi Kapoor: Ravi, data eng, I'll own the pilot work.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Great, thanks — excited to dig in. We got your pre-call note about 500 qps target, 1M vectors, and hybrid search needs, is that still accurate?
[00:31] Marta Lopez: Yep that's accurate. Our current infra is Elastic for term search and a small Pinecone PoC for embeddings, but latency and costs are creeping up.
[00:40] Evan Rogers: Understood. High-level, Redwood offers hosted API and also dedicated pools and private VPC options. For embedding + rerank flows we commonly see a two-stage architecture: sparse retrieval (BM25) to get candidates, then embedding ANN to expand, and optional cross-encoder rerank for top K.
[00:56] Tom Cheng: Quick question — can we keep our Elastic cluster and just call Redwood for embeddings, or do you want us to move vectors into your managed DB?
[01:06] Priya Nair: You can do either. Many customers keep Elastic for sparse retrieval and store vectors in their own vector DB (Milvus/Weaviate/Pinecone) while calling Redwood's hosted embeddings. If you want unified management and lower ops, Redwood Dedicated or Hosted + Redis-like vector caching can be used. There's tradeoffs on egress and latency.
[01:26] Ravi Kapoor: We're sensitive about data residency and encryption. If we send PII-ish descriptions to hosted embeddings, what are the guarantees?
[01:34] Evan Rogers: Good point. Our hosted API supports optional customer-managed keys (KMS) for encryption at rest for Dedicated/Private; hosted still encrypts in transit and at rest but for regulated data many choose Dedicated with KMS and VPC peering or Private on-prem. We can share the SOC2 cert and security whitepaper after the call.
[01:52] Marta Lopez: For model selection, we saw recommendations for 1536-d embeddings vs 768. Our queries are short: pickup/dropoff addresses, short natural language. Any guidance?
[02:02] Priya Nair: 1536 usually gives better semantic separation for diverse corpora, but 768 can be faster and cheaper. With your scale (1M vectors), 1536 at 500 qps is doable on dedicated pools but costs will be higher. We often recommend running a small A/B: sample 100k vectors at both dims to measure recall/latency.
[02:24] Tom Cheng: What's typical RPS we need to provision on dedicated? If we want 500 qps bursty with p95 latency under 100ms for ANN lookup?
[02:33] Priya Nair: Depends on batch sizes and whether you do CPU-based or GPU-backed ANN. Redwood Dedicated GPUs with an ANN engine can handle 500 qps with p95 ~60-120ms for single-vector queries; batching and KV cache reduce cost. We'll include sample throughput numbers in the playbook.
[02:50] Ravi Kapoor: We're also considering hybrid search — BM25 first then ANN on top. How do you recommend tuning cutoff sizes (k1)?
[02:59] Priya Nair: Typical flow: BM25 top 200 -> ANN expand to top 500 -> cross-encoder rerank top 10. Cutoffs depend on recall vs latency; for logistics short queries, BM25 often has high precision so you might start with top 100. We can tune in the pilot.
[03:17] Marta Lopez: Integration-wise, if we keep vectors in-house (Milvus), do you have an SDK or does Redwood return embeddings only?
[03:25] Evan Rogers: Redwood returns embeddings via API/SDK; customers then upsert to their vector DB. We also provide connectors and example pipelines for Milvus/Weaviate/Pinecone, and telemetry hooks to correlate model/prompt versions with retrieval quality.
[03:37] Tom Cheng: Any offline index building we need to worry about? Re-index times for 1M vectors?
[03:44] Priya Nair: Index build time depends on index type and compute. GPU-accelerated indexing can be significantly faster. We'll detail recommended index types (IVF, HNSW) and expected build times for 1M in the benchmark doc.
[03:58] Marta Lopez: On the ranking stage — we expect to run a cross-encoder rerank for final top-10, would that run on Redwood too? Latency concern.
[04:06] Priya Nair: Yes, you can run cross-encoder models on Redwood with low-latency configurations; for strict latency SLOs some customers run the cross-encoder on Dedicated GPUs or run smaller distilled models. There's also the option of using a cheap model for re-ranking and doing full cross-encoder only for fallback in highest-sensitivity flows.
[04:25] Ravi Kapoor: Cost ballpark — hosted embeddings for 1M vectors with 500 qps, estimated monthly?
[04:32] Evan Rogers: We'll send a sample calc but rough guestimate: hosted embeddings only is often lower up-front; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and can be cheaper at scale depending on commit. We'll include both examples in the follow-up.
[04:44] Marta Lopez: For the pilot success criteria — we want recall@10 > 0.8 for routing queries and end-to-end p95 < 200ms for user-facing flows. Is that realistic?
[04:55] Priya Nair: That seems reasonable as a target. We'll build the pilot to aim for those metrics and include AB test plan.
[05:03] Tom Cheng: What's typical lead time for Private (on-prem) deployment?
[05:08] Evan Rogers: Private deployments are usually 6-8 weeks depending on networking and procurement, Dedicated can be faster if you're comfortable with hosted control plane + VPC peering. We'll map this in the follow-up.
[05:19] Marta Lopez: Ok can we talk about telemetry — we need to tie query logs back to model versions and have audit logs for rerank decisions.
[05:27] Priya Nair: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. For audit logs we can stream to your logging endpoint or S3 for retention. We'll include an example retention policy.
[05:40] Ravi Kapoor: Dev integration: how much code to swap our current pipeline?
[05:44] Evan Rogers: Minimal for embeddings-only: call Redwood embed -> upsert to your vector DB -> query flow same. If you adopt Redwood managed vector store, there is more integration but fewer moving parts. Priya will send example code snippets.
[05:56] Marta Lopez: Any surprises re: dimensionality and metric type? cosine vs dot product?
[06:01] Priya Nair: Cosine is common; dot product sometimes used depending on model. We'll recommend based on embedding model chosen. Also if you quantize (int8), we'll note any accuracy impacts.
[06:12] Tom Cheng: Are there SLA differences between hosted and dedicated?
[06:16] Evan Rogers: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted is best-effort with usage-based pricing. For enterprise we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[06:26] Marta Lopez: Security again: do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[06:30] Evan Rogers: Customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we have encryption at rest but KMS for hosted is limited — we'll clarify in the security doc.
[06:40] Priya Nair: Ok, let's walk through a proposed pilot scope: 1) sample 100k vectors test at 768 vs 1536 dims to measure recall/latency; 2) run 1M vector index build + 24hr throughput test at 500 qps; 3) evaluate hybrid BM25+ANN with cross-encoder rerank on top-10. Pilot duration ~2-3 weeks.
[07:02] Ravi Kapoor: Sounds good. For pilot infra, we prefer to keep vectors in-house initially. We'd like Redwood to provide embeddings and run the reranker; we'll handle ANN with Milvus. Is that supported?
[07:14] Priya Nair: Yes, that's a common pattern: we will provide embeddings and you run ANN, and Redwood SE will help coordinate the benchmark. If later you want Redwood-managed vector store or Dedicated, we can migrate.
[07:26] Marta Lopez: Any constraints on embeddings throughput? Our ingestion pipeline will push 10k vectors/hour for the initial sync and then stream updates.
[07:34] Evan Rogers: Hosted API rate limits apply but can be raised; Dedicated or Private avoids noisy-neighbor limits. We'll note ingestion best-practices in the playbook.
[07:45] Tom Cheng: For observability — can Redwood correlate embedding version with rerank metrics?
[07:50] Priya Nair: Yes, we capture model_id and embedding_version in logs and Console shows per-model performance. We'll include a sample dashboard export.
[07:59] Marta Lopez: Ok, final things — procurement: do you need a PO for pilot?
[08:03] Evan Rogers: For a short proof-of-concept we can usually run a limited pilot under our trial terms; procurement kicks in for Dedicated/Private. We'll follow up with the legal checklist.
[08:14] Ravi Kapoor: Thanks all.
[08:16] Evan Rogers: Great, recap of next steps: I'll send pricing, Priya will share benchmark docs and sample scripts, Ravi will provide sample data and QPS patterns. We'll schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[08:28] Marta Lopez: Thanks, appreciate it.
[08:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional words garbled (e.g., "KV cache" heard as "KV case"), slight speaker overlap around 07:00 mark.
final_recap: Agreed pilot plan: 100k dim comparison + 1M benchmark at 500 qps; Redwood to provide pricing, benchmark playbook, and security docs; Astra to provide sample data and confirm compliance needs. Target pilot kickoff week of 2026-10-20.
